question: Fix d>=3. A d-dimensional Werner state has parameter alpha in [-1,1] and is k-extendible exactly when alpha >= (1-d)/k. An isotropic state has valid parameter x>=0 and is k-extendible exactly when x >= [d/(d+1)](1-1/k), for positive integers k. Using these given criteria, prove every Werner state is2-extendible, determine the largest k for a fixed isotropic x below d/(d+1), and find the two parameter thresholds for extendibility at every k. Explain why the numerator grouping in (1-d)/k is essential.
reference_answer: For Werner states and k=2, (1-d)/2<=-1 because d>=3. Every allowed alpha>=-1 therefore satisfies the2-extendibility criterion. The thresholds (1-d)/k increase toward0 as k grows, since1-d<0. Thus satisfying every k is equivalent to alpha>=0: if alpha<0 a sufficiently large k violates the inequality. For isotropic states write c=d/(d+1)>0. The criterion x>=c(1-1/k) is equivalent to1/k>=1-x/c. For0<=x<c this right side is positive, so precisely the integers1<=k<=1/(1-x/c) are allowed; the largest is the floor of that real bound. If x>=c, every k satisfies the inequality. Hence all-k thresholds are alpha>=0 and x>=d/(d+1). This calculation uses (1-d)/k, not1-d/k. The latter tends to1 instead of0 and gives a different, false criterion for this parameterization. These conclusions follow from the stated analytic criteria, not from a new proof of the upstream extendibility theorem.

question: Let |Phi+> = (1/sqrt(d)) sum_{i=1}^d |i>_A |i>_B be the standard maximally entangled state on C^d tensor C^d. (a) Prove the transpose trick: for every operator X in L(C^d), (X_A tensor I_B)|Phi+> = (I_A tensor X^T_B)|Phi+>, where X^T is the transpose of X in the fixed computational basis. (b) Deduce that |Phi+> is invariant under every unitary of the form U tensor conj(U) (U_A tensor the complex conjugate of U on B). Carefully state the role of the computational basis in defining the transpose and conjugate.
reference_answer: Expand the left side: (X tensor I)|Phi>=(1/sqrt d)sum_{i,j}X(j,i)|j> tensor|i>. Expanding (I tensor X^T)|Phi> gives(1/sqrt d)sum_{i,j}X(i,j)|i> tensor|j>; interchanging dummy indices yields the same vector. For a unitary U, apply that identity with X=U and then apply I tensor bar U: (U tensor bar U)|Phi>=(I tensor bar U U^T)|Phi>. Since UU dagger=I, taking entrywise complex conjugates gives bar U U^T=I. The vector is therefore unchanged. Both transpose and bar refer to the same fixed orthonormal basis used to define|Phi>. In contrast U tensor U does not generally fix this vector: for d2 and U=diag(1,i), (|00>+|11>)/sqrt2 becomes(|00>-|11>)/sqrt2. Thus conjugation on the second factor is essential, not a removable notation convention.

question: Let H=C^d with d>=1, and integers M>=N>=1. Let Pi_L project onto the symmetric subspace of H tensor L and d_L its dimension. Define T(X)=(d_N/d_M)Pi_M(X tensor I^{tensor(M-N)})Pi_M. Prove T is completely positive and derive the exact trace formula tr T(X)=tr(X Pi_N) for every positive X. You may use Pi_L=d_L times the Haar average of|phi><phi| tensor L over unit vectors. Characterize trace preservation for positive X and show why it includes more than mixtures of pure tensor powers.
reference_answer: Choose an orthonormal basis e_j of the ancillary tensor factors and insertion maps K_j:v->v tensor e_j. Then sum_j K_j X K_j dagger=X tensor I, so this map is completely positive; generally it needs several Kraus maps, not one isometry. Compression Y->Pi_M Y Pi_M is also completely positive, and positive scaling preserves that property. Let Q be the partial trace of Pi_M over the last M-N factors. The given Haar identity gives Q=d_M integral |phi><phi| tensor N=(d_M/d_N)Pi_N, because each traced pure projector has trace1. Cyclicity and Pi_M squared=Pi_M yield tr T(X)=(d_N/d_M)tr[(X tensor I)Pi_M]=(d_N/d_M)tr(XQ)=tr(X Pi_N)<=tr X. Equality holds exactly when tr[X(I-Pi_N)]=0. For X>=0 this is equivalent to support(X) contained in the symmetric subspace: the positive square-root identity tr[X(I-Pi_N)]=||(I-Pi_N)X^(1/2)||_HS^2 gives the equivalence. Every mixture of pure powers lies there, but not every symmetric state is such a mixture. For d2,N2, the entangled vector(|01>+|10>)/sqrt2 is symmetric, so its projector preserves trace under T, yet it is not a mixture of pure powers (a pure entangled state cannot be a convex combination of product pure states). Thus support in Sym^N, not separability into pure powers, is the correct equality condition.
